findings.explanation: The new GET /orders/<int:order_id> endpoint applies only @require_auth and returns order.to_dict() for any order_id supplied by the requester, with no ownership verification. security-policy.md §3 explicitly requires that 'Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data,' and api-spec.md lists '/orders/<id> GET' as 'owner or admin'. The code never calls is_owner_or_admin (which is imported at line 13 and used correctly in app/routes/users.py:32,45), so any authenticated user can read any other user's order by guessing/enumerating the integer id — a classic IDOR.

evidence.content: A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id)` before returning data.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an ownership check before returning data, mirroring app/routes/users.py: after fetching the order, do `if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, order.user_id): return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403` (and ideally return 403/404 before exposing existence). Ensure the Order model exposes user_id for the check.
